To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Pol λ and Polβ catalyze gap filling with high efficiency and fidelity when the gap is short, and Pol λ is more error prone than Polβ during gap filling with a long gap.

human DNA polymerases β and λ have distinct gap-filling DNA polymerase activities that are dependent upon the gap size, and Pol λ, unlike Pol β, has a threshold on gap size for efficient gap-filling DNA.

the catalytic efficiency of human Pol λ and Pol λ truncation mutants for dNTP incorporation decreased as a function of gap size, whereas the catalytic fidelity decreased with increasing gap size only for the N-terminal domain truncations of Pol λ, and that the N-terminal domains of Pol λ controlled its catalytic fidelity during long gap-filing DNA synthesis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the catalytic efficiency, fidelity, and substrate specificity of DNA polymerases during gap-filling synthesis and the implications for the BER pathway.
how DNA polymerases can efficiently and accurately fill gaps in DNA and how the fidelity of these enzymes is regulated by the size of the gap and the identity of the 5'-flanking base.
how Pol λ and Pol λ N-terminal domains contribute to its catalytic efficiency and base substitution fidelity during gap-filling synthesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Pol λ and Pol λ N-terminal domain truncations are more error-prone during gap-filling synthesis than Pol β and that Pol λ is more error-prone for longer gaps.
Pol λ, like other DNA polymerases, has its own unique catalytic properties that are dependent upon its specific DNA substrate.
Pol λ and Polβ both have a high catalytic efficiency and low base substitution fidelity during gap-filling synthesis, which would be advantageous for the repair of DNA lesions that occur in vivo.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Pol λ and Pol λ N-terminal domain truncations have similar base substitution fidelity when the gap size is ≤ 5 nucleotides.
the efficiency and fidelity of human Pol λ and Polβ during gap-filling synthesis is dependent upon the gap size and the identity of the template and primer bases.
the fidelity of a polymerase during gap filling is not solely determined by the identity of the 3'-OH primer terminus but rather is dependent upon the identity and length of the DNA gap.
The main takeaway from our work is that
both Pol λ, as well as Pol β, can catalyze gap filling DNA synthesis with high efficiency and fidelity when the DNA substrate is short.
the fidelity of Pol λ is highly sensitive to its DNA substrate, which may have important implications for its function during BER and other DNA repair pathways in vivo.
Pol λ, in contrast to Pol β, is a less accurate polymerase for gap-filling DNA during BER, and this may be a consequence of its non-enzymes N-terminal domains.
